notes.note: Photo-judging pass on Budapest and Copenhagen, session with working egress, one image request every 3.2 seconds and no 429. 14 images viewed as pixels (bud_004 x3, bud_006 x1, bud_007 x7, bud_008 x2, cop_005 x1); bud_001, bud_002 and bud_003 were already closed by the 2026-08-08 pass and were not re-judged. Zero approvals. One hold: bud_008 frame Budapest, arboles 1988 03, which is the only image in the whole batch that meets the Cadiz composition test, correctly identified by the uploader as the old black locust of Szechenyi Istvan ter, and fails only on being an August 1988 slide with period cars in frame. The pattern across both cities is that Commons geosearch returns the building rather than the tree: seven apartment-block interiors for the Karolyi kert mulberry, a street sign for the Copenhagen ginkgo, a Judas tree flower close-up for the Fuveszkert cherry. The Taban trail candidates are a specific trap worth remembering: correctly named Morus alba on the correct nature trail, 80m from our pin, and all young staked plantings rather than the veteran. Budapest and Copenhagen both still publish zero photographs; these gaps are now documented dead ends on Commons and should not be re-swept.

Photo-judging pass on Boston, Chicago and Athens, local session, throttled to one image request every 3.2 seconds across 21 fetches with no rate limiting. 21 previously unjudged images viewed as pixels (chi_001 12, ath_011 4, ath_012 5) and all 21 rejected, so no photo was approved and Boston and Chicago still publish zero. The brief listed 11 further Boston candidates, but bos_001, bos_003, bos_004 and bos_005 already carried verdicts from the 2026-08-08 pass and were not re-judged. What the pixels show: the Commons geosearch on the Midway is entirely University of Chicago quadrangle architecture plus oaks grouped behind hedges, and the Plaka sweep for ath_012 is night and dusk street photography. The one near miss is ath_011, a good daylight palm portrait that is 118 m inside the National Garden rather than at the Amalias entrance and is identified as Washingtonia robusta against that entry's filifera, which is also a species discrepancy worth a verification look. chi_001, ath_011, ath_012, bos_001 and bos_004 are now closed out; every tree in this batch has zero unjudged candidates left.

Photo-judging pass, session with working egress, throttled to one image request every three seconds and no rate limiting hit. 37 images viewed as pixels across the rollout cities (Barcelona, Rome, Edinburgh, Amsterdam, Berlin, Lisbon, Genoa): 31 Commons, 5 iNaturalist, 1 Openverse. One approved (bcn_013, the catalogued Maclura of the Ciutadella). The Commons geosearch lane is now almost pure noise for these cities: street corners, facades, a Vespa, a stage screen, a sarcophagus and a street cleaning truck. Rome rom_011 is the near miss, the correct tree per Wikidata coordinates but photographed from above with the crown merged into surrounding canopy. Whole-city verdicts: Barcelona, Rome, Edinburgh, Amsterdam, Berlin, Lisbon and Genoa now have no unjudged candidates left, so their remaining photo gaps need a new source, not another sweep.

Photo-judging pass. Only inaturalist-open-data.s3.amazonaws.com was reachable this run: upload.wikimedia.org and api.openverse.org are both refused by the egress proxy (403 on CONNECT), so 310 Commons candidates and all 18 wikidata ones, plus the 3 openverse ones, could not be rendered and were left unjudged rather than approved blind.

Photo-judging pass with working egress. upload.wikimedia.org was reachable (the 2026-08-07 note was a GitHub Actions proxy block, not a dead host); it rate-limits at roughly 1 request per 3 seconds. 29 images rendered and viewed, 5 approved (ber_013, bat_002, bel_001, bel_003, bel_004). Correction to the standing brief: the 19 wikidata candidates were already judged on 2026-08-07 (12 approved, 6 rejected); only ber_013 was outstanding. Barcelona and Rome are exhausted, every remaining unjudged tree in both has zero candidates.

Photo-judging pass, scheduled routine, remote session (not GitHub Actions). upload.wikimedia.org and api.openverse.org both refused (403 on CONNECT via the environment's egress proxy), same policy block as the CI runner. inaturalist-open-data.s3.amazonaws.com was reachable, so this pass judged the 20 reachable iNaturalist candidates across 8 trees with no prior outcome (Barcelona x9 across 3 trees, Edinburgh, Geneva x2, Groningen, Krakow, Malaga): all 20 rejected, leaf/fruit/bark/hand close-ups or backlit canopy shots with no readable trunk. bcn_002, bcn_013, edi_007 and kra_003 each still carry one unreached Wikimedia or Openverse candidate and stay open rather than closed out. Four other candidates in the queue (lis_013, mad_002, mil_011, prg_012) were already judged on 2026-08-07 by an earlier pass (held/rejected); this pass checked candidate-level `judged` fields before viewing anything and left those calls untouched rather than re-judging blind.

Photo-judging pass, scheduled routine. Checked both candidate-level `judged` and tree-level `judged`/`outcome` fields (the earlier same-day pass only checked the former, which would have re-judged ber_013 and lei_005 blind since both are already resolved at the tree level: ber_013 approved via a Wikidata/Wikimedia candidate, lei_005 rejected outright). After that correction, zero candidates in the queue are both unjudged and reachable: the only reachable host is inaturalist-open-data.s3.amazonaws.com, and every iNaturalist candidate in the queue already carries a judged verdict, at either the candidate or tree level. upload.wikimedia.org and api.openverse.org (380 and 4 unjudged candidates respectively) remain fully unreachable this session; confirmed via the agent proxy status endpoint as policy denials (403 on CONNECT), not a rate limit or transient failure. No photos judged this pass; none were available to judge.

Photo-judging pass on the rollout cities (Dublin, New York, Paris). 30 images downloaded and viewed as pixels, throttled to one request every 3.2 seconds with no rate limiting. One approved: nyc_011, the Great Elm of Central Park West, from a CC0 iNaturalist observation whose reverse-geocoded place is literally Central Park West/W 77 St and whose photograph shows the wide low-spreading crown the entry describes. dub_005 (the Provost's Plane) is now exhausted: all ten Commons geosearch candidates are Grafton and Suffolk Street scenes, three of them the Molly Malone statue. par_017 (the Anne Frank Chestnut, Jardin Anne Frank, Paris) is closed out without pixels and deliberately so: every one of the nine candidates is a documented OTHER Anne Frank tree (Yad Vashem, Bedford, Uedelhoven, Utrecht, Bournemouth, a US exhibit, the fallen Amsterdam original) or a museum object, so the rejection rests on the file's own coordinates and description, which is stronger evidence than a pixel could give. New York's iNaturalist lane is mostly phenology close-ups: buds, bark, leaves in the hand. nyc_009's remaining candidates are Quercus alba observations against a Quercus rubra entry, and nyc_012/nyc_013 share the same five candidates, all rejected.

Photo-judging pass on the top-25 rollout cities (Paris, Rome, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Seville, Edinburgh, Budapest, Athens). 35 images downloaded and viewed as pixels, throttled to one request every 3.2 seconds with no rate limiting. One approved: par_010, the Sophora by the Lake in the Parc des Buttes-Chaumont, a CC BY 4.0 photograph whose own GPS lands 22 m from our pin and which carries the city's 'Sophora remarquable' panel in frame. 83 candidates across 32 trees are now judged and 31 of those trees are closed out as exhausted. The dominant failure is that the Commons geosearch and iNaturalist lanes for these cities return proximity, not subject: street corners, a Vespa, a museum sarcophagus, a giant chessboard, a concert portrait of a man named Matthew Tree, and phenology close-ups of leaves, pods and flower spikes. Two near misses worth recording: edi_010's Corstorphine Sycamore photograph is excellent but is the Royal Botanic Garden specimen, a different individual 8 km from our churchyard pin, and rom_011's Villa Sciarra cedar is the correct tree shot from above the crown with no trunk visible. Athens ath_010's eleven candidates are one Ameriki Square series; four were viewed and the series closed on that evidence.

notes: 2026-08-08 US federal-source sweep (photo-judge): HALS/Library of Congress witness-tree documentation (HALS DC-6 bur oak, DC-7 Jefferson elm, DC-9 botanic garden elm) is public domain and identity-perfect, but it is black and white large-format archival photography and therefore fails the Cadiz standard; do not re-hunt it. Architect of the Capitol imagery is disqualified by AOC's own non-commercial terms ('educational, scholarly, news or personal purposes'), whatever the Flickr 'United States Government Work' tag says. NPS npgallery uploads on Commons photograph memorials and buildings, not individual trees.

notes.note: Baarn viewing pass, manual Dutch-term hunt after the API sweep returned zero candidates for all five trees. Swept Commons categories (Cantonspark, Kasteel Groeneveld and its Gardens/Icehouse subcategories, Parks in Baarn, Nature of Baarn), Commons geosearch on all three sites, 25 Dutch and English Commons searches, Openverse across five terms, and iNaturalist within 5 km. 40 images rendered and viewed as pixels: 34 Commons, 6 Flickr CC BY. Zero approvals. iNaturalist is a dead end for Baarn: every observation of Metasequoia, Sequoiadendron, Quercus rubra, Fagus sylvatica and Liriodendron in range is CC BY-NC or unlicensed. The pattern across all five trees is the same, these parks are photographed as places (wintertuin, colonnade, ice cellar, castle facade, moat) and never as trees.
